submission.justification: Module-D2 at 30% wall coverage achieves the highest light collection (36.973 PE/MeV) among designs that meet all requirements. While Module-D1 would provide superior light collection (52.977 PE/MeV), it has a 30% failure rate in thermal cycling tests, which is 6 times higher than the maximum allowed 5%. Since modules are inaccessible once the cryostat is filled, reliability is critical. Module-D2 has only a 2% failure rate, well within the requirement, and delivers 52% more light than Module-D3 (24.403 PE/MeV at the same coverage). The 30% coverage maximizes light collection within the allowed range (5-30%) and is supported by available feedthroughs as confirmed in the meeting notes.

requirements.requirement: Module must be one of the three designs listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Module-D2 is one of the three candidate designs: wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout.

requirements.requirement: At most 5% of modules may fail after 20 thermal cycles (300 K to 87 K)
requirements.evidence: Thermal cycling tests show Module-D2 has a 2% failure rate, which is below the 5% maximum. Module-D1 (30% failure) and Module-D3 (0.5% failure) were also tested, but only D2 and D3 meet this requirement.
Recommended coverage of 30% is at the upper limit of the allowed range. Meeting notes confirm sufficient feedthroughs are available for up to 30% coverage.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible light collection (photoelectrons per MeV)
requirements.evidence: Simulation shows Module-D2 at 30% coverage achieves 36.973 PE/MeV, which is the highest light collection among designs that meet the thermal cycling reliability requirement. Module-D1 would achieve higher (52.977 PE/MeV) but fails the thermal cycling constraint.
